title: Ministerial Declaration of the 2024 High-Level Segment on Reinforcing the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and Eradicating Poverty
executive_summary: The 2024 ministerial declaration from the UN Economic and Social Council and High-Level Political Forum reaffirms global commitment to the 2030 Agenda and its 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), emphasizing urgent action to eradicate poverty amid multiple crises. It highlights challenges including climate change, conflicts, inequalities, and the COVID-19 aftermath, stressing the need for peace, inclusive societies, and sustainable economic growth. The declaration calls for enhanced international cooperation, increased financing, and support for vulnerable groups and developing countries. Key priorities include climate action aligned with the Paris Agreement, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture, and strengthening governance and institutions. It underscores the importance of gender equality, digital inclusion, and data-driven policymaking. The declaration supports reforming international financial systems, scaling up development finance, and improving debt mechanisms. It encourages voluntary national reviews to monitor progress and stresses multi-stakeholder engagement to accelerate SDG implementation, aiming for a just, resilient, and inclusive world by 2030.
characteristics: The declaration reaffirms commitment to the 2030 Agenda and its 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), emphasizing urgency, inclusivity, and leaving no one behind, especially the most vulnerable.
It highlights multiple global crises including climate change, conflicts, pandemics, and inequalities as major challenges to sustainable development and poverty eradication.
The declaration stresses the importance of peace, good governance, human rights, gender equality, and inclusive institutions as foundations for sustainable development.
It calls for enhanced international cooperation, increased financing, technology transfer, and capacity-building to support developing countries and address financing gaps.
Specific goals addressed include ending poverty and hunger, combating climate change, promoting peaceful societies, and strengthening global partnerships for sustainable development.

The declaration encourages the use of science, technology, innovation, and data to accelerate progress and calls for strengthened voluntary national reviews and stakeholder participation in SDG implementation.
practical_applications: Full implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, including capacity-building and technical and financial assistance for developing countries, promotion of disaster risk-informed sustainable development, and multi-hazard early warning mechanisms.

Mobilization of financial resources to close the biodiversity financing gap and support the implementation of the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

Support for the global efforts to address plastic pollution, including the work of the intergovernmental negotiating committee to develop an international legally binding instrument on plastic pollution by the end of 2024.
Strengthening social protection systems and expanding coverage of social protection programs to reduce poverty and hunger.
Implementation of the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions.

Promotion of sustainable, efficient, inclusive, and resilient agrifood systems, including support for family farming, reduction of food loss and waste, integrated water resources management, and safe, nutritious school feeding programs.
Development and application of science, technology, and innovation in agriculture, including use of advanced information technologies to support smallholder and family farmers.

Operationalization of funding arrangements for loss and damage associated with climate change, including the Fund established under UNFCCC decisions 1/CP.28 and 5/CMA.5, with pledges of financial support.
Support for the Santiago network for averting, minimizing, and addressing loss and damage from climate change.
Scaling up international public finance and improved access to concessional finance for developing countries to address financing gaps for the Sustainable Development Goals.
Promotion of reform of the international financial architecture and international financial institutions to better address global challenges and support SDG investments.
Improved international debt mechanisms, including debt review, debt payment suspensions, debt restructuring, and scaling up debt swaps for SDGs, climate, nature, and food security.
Voluntary rechanneling of special drawing rights (SDRs) to countries most in need through multilateral development banks.
Preparations for the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development in 2025 to assess progress and address financing challenges.
Implementation of integrated national financing frameworks aligned with nationally owned sustainable development strategies.
Strengthening international tax cooperation, including support for the UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation.
Promotion of investment and development of project pipelines and bankable projects, with technical assistance and capacity-building support.

Advancement of innovative solutions to unlock SDG investments, including the Sustainable Development Goals Investment Fair, Global Pilot Programme on Science, Technology and Innovation for the SDGs Road Maps, and the United Nations Global Compact.
Expansion of digital infrastructure connectivity, capacity building, and access to technological innovations to bridge digital divides and enhance participation in the digital economy.
Strengthening data systems to collect high-quality, timely, relevant, disaggregated, and reliable data on SDG progress, including financing and capacity-building support for developing countries.
Encouragement of countries to develop national road maps for voluntary national reviews (VNRs) and support local authorities in preparing voluntary local reviews.
Strengthening the quality of voluntary national reviews through evidence-based participatory processes, use of accurate and comparable data, anticipatory models, and inclusion of statistical annexes.
commitments: Achieve the vision of a sustainable, resilient, prosperous, peaceful, just and inclusive world by 2030, as envisioned in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
Full implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030.
Mobilize financial resources to close the biodiversity financing gap for the effective implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
Support the development and adoption of an international legally binding instrument on plastic pollution, including in the marine environment, by the end of 2024.
Implement the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals with bold, ambitious, accelerated, just and transformative action in the six years leading up to 2030.
Strengthen social protection systems and expand coverage of social protection programmes to reduce poverty and hunger.
Eradicate forced labour, human trafficking, and end child labour in all its forms.
End hunger, food insecurity and all forms of malnutrition by 2030 through sustainable, efficient, inclusive and resilient agrifood systems.
Reduce global carbon dioxide emissions by 43% by 2030 relative to the 2019 level and achieve net zero emissions by or around mid-century.
Set a new collective quantified climate finance goal from a floor of 100 billion US dollars per year at the 29th session of the Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC.

Developed countries to fulfill official development assistance commitments, including 0.7% of gross national income (GNI) for ODA to developing countries and 0.15 to 0.20% of ODA/GNI to least developed countries.
Support the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development to be held from 30 June to 3 July 2025.
Strengthen data and statistical capacities in developing countries, increase financing for data and statistics, and enhance capacity-building support to close Sustainable Development Goal data gaps.
Encourage countries to develop national road maps of voluntary national reviews for presentation until 2030 and support local authorities in preparing voluntary local reviews.

kpi_list.kpi_text: We strongly reaffirm our commitment to building a sustainable, resilient, prosperous, peaceful, just and inclusive world by 2030, as envisioned in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
kpi_list.target_description: Build a sustainable, resilient, prosperous, peaceful, just and inclusive world by 2030
kpi_list.measurement_method: Assessment of progress on the 17 SDGs through national and global monitoring frameworks

kpi_list.kpi_text: We recommit to the full implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, and recall its midterm review, as disasters have become more frequent and intense.
kpi_list.target_description: Full implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring of disaster risk reduction policies and integration into national and local development plans
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States and relevant disaster risk reduction bodies

kpi_list.kpi_text: We will support the global efforts to address plastic pollution, and the work of the intergovernmental negotiating committee to develop an international legally binding instrument on plastic pollution, including in the marine environment, by the end of 2024.
kpi_list.target_description: Develop an international legally binding instrument on plastic pollution
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption of the legally binding instrument by the intergovernmental negotiating committee

kpi_list.kpi_text: We reaffirm the Paris Agreement temperature goal of holding the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels... including reducing global carbon dioxide emissions, by 43 per cent by 2030 relative to the 2019 level, and to net zero by or around mid-century.
kpi_list.target_description: Reduce global carbon dioxide emissions by 43% relative to 2019 levels
kpi_list.measurement_method: Global greenhouse gas emissions inventories and reporting under UNFCCC
kpi_list.responsible_entity: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Parties

kpi_list.kpi_text: We reaffirm our resolve to set, at the twenty-ninth session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, a new collective quantified goal from a floor of 100 billion dollars per year, taking into account the needs and priorities of developing countries.
kpi_list.target_description: Mobilize at least 100 billion USD per year for climate finance
kpi_list.measurement_method: Financial reporting and pledges tracking under UNFCCC mechanisms

kpi_list.kpi_text: We urge developed countries to scale up and fulfil their respective official development assistance commitments, including the commitment by many developed countries to achieve the target of 0.7 per cent of gross national income for official development assistance (ODA/GNI) to developing countries and 0.15 to 0.20 per cent of ODA/GNI to the least developed countries.
kpi_list.metric_name: Official Development Assistance (ODA) to GNI Ratio
kpi_list.target_description: Achieve 0.7% of GNI as ODA to developing countries
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring of ODA contributions reported by donor countries

kpi_list.kpi_text: We commit to strengthen social protection systems and expand coverage of social protection programmes, to reduce poverty and hunger.
kpi_list.target_description: Strengthen and expand social protection systems to reduce poverty and hunger
kpi_list.measurement_method: National social protection coverage and impact assessments

kpi_list.kpi_text: We commit to eradicate forced labour and human trafficking and end child labour in all its forms.
kpi_list.metric_name: Eradication of Forced Labour, Human Trafficking and Child Labour
kpi_list.target_description: Eradicate forced labour, human trafficking and child labour in all forms
kpi_list.measurement_method: National and international reporting on labour standards and trafficking
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States and International Labour Organization

kpi_list.kpi_text: We will continue to take action to bridge the digital divides and spread the benefits of digitalization. We will expand participation of all countries, in particular developing countries, in the digital economy, including by enhancing their digital infrastructure connectivity, building their capacities and access to technological innovations through stronger partnerships and improving digital literacy.
kpi_list.metric_name: Digital Divide Reduction and Digital Economy Participation
kpi_list.target_description: Bridge digital divides and expand participation in the digital economy, especially for developing countries
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring digital infrastructure, connectivity, literacy and participation rates
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States, International Organizations, Private Sector

kpi_list.kpi_text: We commit to take action to strengthen international, national and local data systems efforts to collect high-quality, timely, relevant, disaggregated and reliable data on Sustainable Development Goals progress and to intensify efforts to strengthen data and statistical capacities in developing countries.
kpi_list.metric_name: Strengthening Data Systems for SDG Monitoring
kpi_list.target_description: Enhance data collection and statistical capacities for SDG progress monitoring
kpi_list.measurement_method: Assessment of data quality, availability, and use in SDG reporting
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States, National Statistical Offices, UN Statistical Commission

sdg_alignment: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

top_actors.name: United Nations
top_actors.justification: The United Nations is the primary actor convening the high-level political forum and Economic and Social Council session, setting the agenda, and driving the implementation of the 2030 Agenda and Sustainable Development Goals. The text repeatedly references UN frameworks, resolutions, and initiatives, highlighting its central role in global governance, coordination, and financing.

top_actors.name: Governments
top_actors.justification: Governments are the main implementers of the 2030 Agenda and Sustainable Development Goals at the national level. The text emphasizes the role of ministers, high representatives, and national policies, including voluntary national reviews, highlighting governments' responsibility and influence in achieving sustainable development targets.

top_actors.name: World Bank
top_actors.justification: The World Bank is explicitly mentioned as a key multilateral development bank involved in financing, capacity-building, and supporting infrastructure investments critical to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. Its participation in the high-level political forum and role in addressing financing gaps and innovative solutions underscores its importance.

top_themes.name: Digital Inclusion
top_themes.justification: Digital inclusion is central to the document's emphasis on leaving no one behind, empowering vulnerable groups, and ensuring equitable access to technology and services. It is repeatedly linked to social protection, gender equality, and bridging divides, making it strategically crucial for achieving the 2030 Agenda.

top_themes.name: Digital Infrastructure
top_themes.justification: The document highlights the need to expand digital infrastructure connectivity, especially in developing countries, as a foundation for digital transformation, economic growth, and social inclusion. It is a key enabler for leveraging technology and innovation to accelerate sustainable development.

top_themes.name: Digital & Technological Partnerships
top_themes.justification: International cooperation and partnerships are emphasized as essential for mobilizing resources, sharing technology, and bridging digital divides. The document stresses multilateralism and global digital cooperation as strategic mechanisms to support digital transformation and sustainable development goals.
